answer: Each agent identity is registered against an enclave’s MRENCLAVE, with a hardware-backed attestation key proving that the measured code runs on genuine SGX or SEV silicon. Copying a VM cannot forge that proof; creating another accepted identity requires access to eligible physical hardware, not merely a hollow software clone. This raises Sybil cost, though MRENCLAVE identifies code, not a unique enclave, so policy must limit repeated registrations. A valid signal, not a gale of self-asserted IDs, establishes trust.
